text:
Predicates:
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Block(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
InClass(x, y) ::: x is in y's class.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Man(x) ∧ Man(y) ∧ Taller(x, y) → Block(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
∀y (Man(michael) ∧ InClass(michael, class) ∧ Taller(michael, y)) ::: Michael is a man who is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z (Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If person x is taller than person y, and person y is taller than person z, than x is taller than z.
Man(peter) ∧ Taller(peter, michael) ::: Peter is a man who is taller than Michael.
∀x (Block(michael, x) ↔ ¬Jump(x)) ::: Michael can block any shooting from a person as long as the person does not jump when shooting.
¬Block(michael, windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.
Conclusion:
∃y (Man(y) ∧ InClass(y, class) ∧ Taller(y, peter)) ::: Peter is shorter than a man in Michael's class.
